target_customer: Pharma and biotech licensees (the plan is to develop through phase 2 then license), and ultimately patients with psoriasis, autoimmune disease and inflammation driven cancers
problem: Autoimmune and chronic inflammatory diseases are treated with immune suppressing drugs; SFA develops oral deuterated short chain fatty acid drugs that regulate rather than suppress the immune system.
business_model: Biotech drug development, license phase 3 ready assets to partners for fees, royalties and milestones

founders.name: Ira Spector
founders.role: Co-founder, CEO (CSO on the company site)
education: Washington University, BS in Physics and EE
previous_startups: Co-founded four startups before SFA (self reported, names not found)
founders.background_notes: 30 plus years in drug development per YC page and Pulse 2.0 interview.

founders.name: Alla Arzumanyan
founders.background_notes: Assistant professor at Temple and co-inventor of SFA002 per YC page.

founders.name: Mark Feitelson
founders.background_notes: Biology professor at Temple and inventor of the platform per the YC page and company site.

competitors.name: Bristol Myers Squibb deucravacitinib (later Sotyktu)
competitors.what: Oral TYK2 inhibitor for plaque psoriasis, tested head to head against Otezla in phase 3
competitors.traction_then: Positive topline phase 3 results announced November 2020 and February 2021

competitors.name: Amgen Otezla (apremilast)
competitors.what: Marketed oral PDE4 inhibitor for psoriasis
competitors.traction_then: On market; comparator in the 2021 BMS trials

technical_complexity.rationale: Drug discovery and clinical development with regulatory trials; years of capital intensive work for a tiny team.

defensibility.rationale: The company cites granted patents and a proprietary deuteration platform; claims are company reported.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The big pharma oral psoriasis drugs went to market (Sotyktu approved September 2022) but are not substitutes by mechanism; no acquirer found for SFA.

market_need_then: Psoriasis and other autoimmune diseases affect large patient populations and oral options were limited; the company cites over 300 million patients with autoimmune diseases.

identity.visual_style: Clinical and scientific with repeated investigational disclaimers
identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific, caveated, tagline Resetting the immune system

brand_strength.rationale: A generic acronym name; sources conflict on whether it stands for short chain fatty acid or founders, so it is recorded as unclear.

outcome_analysis: SFA is a Temple University spinout that raised about 4 million seed in 2022 and a further bridge round, and reports positive phase 1b psoriasis data. It is still seeking a 25 million Series A to run phase 2, so progress is slow and capital constrained, but it has not failed. Its fate depends on phase 2 funding and results.
notes: Seed 4 million and investor list from a Ben Franklin Technology Partners article dated January 2023 ('last year'). A November 2023 bridge of 4.5 million appears in a search summary and one aggregator only, not recorded as a round. Total raised ~9 million is company self reported in a Pulse 2.0 interview. A search summary said the name comes from founders' initials, but opened sources do not explain it, so name_origin is null. Founded 2016 per YC page, 2017 per Pulse 2.0. The company site lists Shawn O'Brien as CEO, differing from the YC page and the interview. Competitors are large pharma programs, not startups.
